                                    "identity_notes": "MREC denotes Sen and Bagchi's 1989 recursive best-first memory-controlled procedure, with an explicitly stored graph and virtual unstored successors, backed-up remaining costs and a separate recursion stack.               "source_limitations": [
                {
                  "id": "L1",
                  "topic": "Deadline CDF polarity conflict",
                  "limitation": "Section2.1 calls Di a deadline CDF, and Eq1 uses1−Di. The later deterministic-deadline paragraph says Di is1 before/on latest_start and0 afterward, which is a decreasing survival-style step rather than a CDF. Both PDFs contain the conflict. Preserve it as a source presentation issue; original2019/2021 equations or versioned implementation are not inspected here, so no implementation defect or silent repair is asserted.",
                  "locator": "Author p.2 Eq1 and p.3 left column after latest_start; official8484–8485",
                  "source": {
                    "path": "/private/tmp/aimech-dispatch-dependent-cope-source-research-20261016/author2025-network.pdf",
                    "sha256": "b81abd754f7becb49d22adce33803c3493512b54aceebf21ff71db93609d4be7"
                  },
                  "status": "explicit source/interpretation boundary, not a canonical defect finding"
                },
                {
                  "id": "L2",
                  "topic": "Success versus failure convention",
                  "limitation": "Eq3 explicitly defines V as probability of success, whereas Section4.1 describes the resulting candidate as failure probability pf. Interpreting pf as1−V matches the described tail of Mi, but no executable formula is printed there. Keep that interpretation explicit, including deadline equality conventions rather than silently treating V itself as the queue’s failure score.",
                  "locator": "Author p.4 Eq3, p.5 Section4.1; official8486–8487",
                  "source": {
                    "path": "/private/tmp/aimech-dispatch-dependent-cope-source-research-20261016/author2025-network.pdf",
                    "sha256": "b81abd754f7becb49d22adce33803c3493512b54aceebf21ff71db93609d4be7"
                  },
                  "status": "explicit source/interpretation boundary, not a canonical defect finding"
                },
                {
                  "id": "L3",
                  "topic": "Frozen-value monotonicity only",
                  "limitation": "For fixed distribution Mi and fixed deadline d, Pr(m<=d−t) is nonincreasing in t. The planner continually updates Mi and deadline/relaxed-plan information; values across those updates need not be monotonic merely because the frozen functional is. Recomputed deadlines also require consistent treatment of time-dependent relaxed plans.",
                  "locator": "Author p.4 Section3 monotonicity paragraph and p.5 periodic refresh; official8486–8487",
                  "source": {
                    "path": "/private/tmp/aimech-dispatch-dependent-cope-source-research-20261016/author2025-network.pdf",

                  },
                  "status": "explicit source/interpretation boundary, not a canonical defect finding"
                },
                {
                  "id": "L4",
                  "topic": "Heuristic prefix reduction",
                  "limitation": "The none/all prefix argument assumes that a reasonable relaxed plan at an ancestor has a successor whose relaxed plan is the matching suffix. It supplies no general optimal-policy proof for inconsistent/changed relaxed plans, discarded ancestors or arbitrary temporal constraints. No theorem of search completeness, optimality or guaranteed successful irreversible dispatch appears in the inspected paper.",
                  "locator": "Author pp.4–5 Section3; Section4 warns bad dispatch may make goals unreachable",
                  "source": {

Admissibility cannot be inferred for an arbitrary first-producer implementation; a fast and a slow producer can require different label handling. This is an exposition/premise limit, not an observed implementation failure.",
            "Earliest-time clamping is justified only with the source’s appropriate complete temporal-window maintenance and its domain assumptions. It is not a generic guarantee for arbitrary CSPs, approximate or stale windows, or an unspecified propagator. The comparison does not demonstrate that a correctly maintained simple temporal network becomes inconsistent merely by earliest-time clamping.",
            "The manually chosen imminence interval assumes sufficient time to plan the next job; the papers discuss interrupting and restarting when needed. Outer-loop temporal updates are restricted to between-job searches, while controller changes can abort a current search. These descriptions do not supply a general hard real-time guarantee or fully specified timeout, unreachable-job and empty-frontier behavior.",
            "The state-uniqueness argument appeals to irreversible logical or resource-order choices reflected in a plan. Local branching distinctions alone do not establish global semantic non-reconvergence, cycle freedom, or a general no-duplicate theorem for arbitrary action domains. No concrete duplicate execution of the authors’ implementation is asserted.",
            "The 2005 simplified rule tests only whether effects match a fully specified state. Full specification plus corresponding effect preconditions does not alone ensure compatibility of preconditions on unaffected atoms. Such a precondition can contradict the target state even when the simplified effect test passes. The earlier general applicability rule retains the needed check; no implementation defect or author erratum is established.",
            "The 2005 simplified update flips added/deleted atoms. That update needs opposite-polarity preconditions for the changed atoms and suitable treatment of other preconditions; the phrase corresponding preconditions does not itself specify those polarities. The general regression update is retained separately, and the simplified branch is not silently strengthened or treated as universally equivalent.",
            "The 2005 paper explicitly supports unknown literals and describes storing true and unknown sets, but later calls the state fully specified and writes a two-set heuristic shorthand. The exact treatment of unknowns in that shorthand remains a source/interface question; this draft does not erase unknowns or claim an implementation-level equivalence of all these descriptions.",
            "The shared procedure is described for the supplied symbolic manufacturing model: jobs are independent except for shared resources and explicit batch constraints, actions for one job are sequential and abut, and controller delay constrains starting times. These restrictions do not establish applicability to arbitrary interacting, stochastic, partially observable or general durative-planning domains.",
            "Representational flexibility is not the same as implemented support: the 2004 paper allows duration ranges but says its implementation uses fixed durations, and it describes additional resource-state compatibility restrictions. These details and the 2005 formal extensions remain version-local; this common record does not equate every modeling option or implementation across the two papers.",
            "The described failure handling assumes reliable transport along planned routes and destination diversion that can discard faulty material; affected jobs can then be replanned from scratch. This does not establish recovery for arbitrary mid-route failures, uncertain state estimation or all in-flight material. Controller-domain changes are handled by aborting the current search under the stated between-search model.",
            "The 2004 experiments distinguish incremental directed path consistency from an arc-consistency variant maintaining origin-relative time windows without adding arcs. The latter does not provide arbitrary pairwise time relations as easily. The comparison does not prove interchangeability of arbitrary AC-3 and IDPC implementations or transfer the reported timing advantage to every domain.",
            "Physical-prototype operation, simulations on selected plant configurations and timing/quality comparisons are separate evidence roles. They do not establish universal throughput, hard deadlines or general optimality. This draft makes no numerical performance claim and has not executed an implementation or reproduced the experiments.",
            "One descriptive identity covers the common outer online coordination and inner temporal/resource regression procedure in these two inspected works, not separately originated A*, STRIPS, STN or propagator components. It does not equate all later printer-planning publications or use the filename token pns as an alias. The 2005 comparison is completed, while remaining cited-original, later-version and implementation questions stay separately tracked."
          ],

      "source_questions": [
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q01",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Static supplied-distribution abstraction; online estimation and integration into a real planner are future work in this paper.",
          "origin": "Official pp.2,8",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q02",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Sequential known-duration base actions and meta-level uncertainty do not cover arbitrary parallel multi-robot or stochastic-action execution.",
          "origin": "Official pp.1,4,8",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q03",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Independence is an analysis premise, not a demonstrated property of real search subtrees; product-failure formulas do not survive arbitrary dependencies.",
          "origin": "Official pp.2–4",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q04",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: With a standard CDF,1−D(t) means deadline>t, whereas the induced-deadline derivation prints start(beta)<=X−R. Discrete equality cases need an explicit convention; no silent off-by-one correction is made.",
          "origin": "Official p.3 Eq1 versus p.4; arXiv p.9",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q05",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: The literal arXiv earliest-time expression adds W and a new computation unit although those can overlap. The W=1, empty-tail, one-unit-remaining-computation hand case finishes atT+1 under the printed state updates but formula givesT+2. This is a source-interface discrepancy, not a diagnosed code defect.",
          "origin": "ArXiv p.9 Appendix A",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q06",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Official Algorithm3 prints no increment in its common-prefix loop, no explicit second-head-length guard and no complete no-mismatch/empty-head convention. Eq7 likewise needs sentinel/empty-set handling for fully compatible heads.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5,7",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q07",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Demand-Execution indexes the head by W[S] in both official and arXiv displays, although W is remaining time and L is initiated-action count. Keep this mismatch explicit rather than inventing an executable replacement.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5,7; arXiv pp.8–10",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q08",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Increasing start times alone do not enforce duration-dependent nonoverlap; Algorithm2 omits an explicit feasibility filter. Algorithm4 subtracts an action entry H[j], requiring duration interpretation; guards for short heads, empty heads and absent support minima are not fully printed.",
          "origin": "Official pp.4,6–7",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q09",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: The reduction helper omits D from its explicit arguments while effective deadlines depend on induced deadlines. Ambient state/distribution access, probability-return contracts and all-zero-success behavior need implementation clarification.",
          "origin": "Official pp.6–7 Algorithms1–5",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q10",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Hazard denominators require unfinished-process positive survival, log-failure utility needs zero/one boundary handling, and LPF/t requires positive allocation time. The formulas are not a complete numerically guarded implementation.",
          "origin": "Official pp.3,5",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q11",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: General CoPE/KID-CoPE are not claimed polynomial-time solvable. The exact cases are pseudo-polynomial in numeric horizons/explicit distributions with bounded-prefix or equal-slack restrictions; bounded truncation in the general case gives up optimality.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5–6",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q12",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: The arXiv proof sketches were read but not formally verified. Their model and interface premises must remain attached; no theorem certification or extension to arbitrary dependencies/continuous time is claimed.",
          "origin": "ArXiv p.9 Appendix B",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null

      "source_questions": [
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q01",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Static supplied-distribution abstraction; online estimation and integration into a real planner are future work in this paper.",
          "origin": "Official pp.2,8",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q02",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Sequential known-duration base actions and meta-level uncertainty do not cover arbitrary parallel multi-robot or stochastic-action execution.",
          "origin": "Official pp.1,4,8",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q03",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Independence is an analysis premise, not a demonstrated property of real search subtrees; product-failure formulas do not survive arbitrary dependencies.",
          "origin": "Official pp.2–4",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q04",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: With a standard CDF,1−D(t) means deadline>t, whereas the induced-deadline derivation prints start(beta)<=X−R. Discrete equality cases need an explicit convention; no silent off-by-one correction is made.",
          "origin": "Official p.3 Eq1 versus p.4; arXiv p.9",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q05",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: The literal arXiv earliest-time expression adds W and a new computation unit although those can overlap. The W=1, empty-tail, one-unit-remaining-computation hand case finishes atT+1 under the printed state updates but formula givesT+2. This is a source-interface discrepancy, not a diagnosed code defect.",
          "origin": "ArXiv p.9 Appendix A",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q06",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Official Algorithm3 prints no increment in its common-prefix loop, no explicit second-head-length guard and no complete no-mismatch/empty-head convention. Eq7 likewise needs sentinel/empty-set handling for fully compatible heads.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5,7",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q07",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Demand-Execution indexes the head by W[S] in both official and arXiv displays, although W is remaining time and L is initiated-action count. Keep this mismatch explicit rather than inventing an executable replacement.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5,7; arXiv pp.8–10",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q08",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Increasing start times alone do not enforce duration-dependent nonoverlap; Algorithm2 omits an explicit feasibility filter. Algorithm4 subtracts an action entry H[j], requiring duration interpretation; guards for short heads, empty heads and absent support minima are not fully printed.",
          "origin": "Official pp.4,6–7",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q09",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: The reduction helper omits D from its explicit arguments while effective deadlines depend on induced deadlines. Ambient state/distribution access, probability-return contracts and all-zero-success behavior need implementation clarification.",
          "origin": "Official pp.6–7 Algorithms1–5",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q10",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: Hazard denominators require unfinished-process positive survival, log-failure utility needs zero/one boundary handling, and LPF/t requires positive allocation time. The formulas are not a complete numerically guarded implementation.",
          "origin": "Official pp.3,5",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null
        },
        {
          "id": "COPE2023-Q11",
          "question": "Clarify or retain: General CoPE/KID-CoPE are not claimed polynomial-time solvable. The exact cases are pseudo-polynomial in numeric horizons/explicit distributions with bounded-prefix or equal-slack restrictions; bounded truncation in the general case gives up optimality.",
          "origin": "Official pp.5–6",
          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",
          "owner": null

          "question": "Clarify or retain: The arXiv proof sketches were read but not formally verified. Their model and interface premises must remain attached; no theorem certification or extension to arbitrary dependencies/continuous time is claimed.",

          "status": "Retained source qualification; no canonical resolution.",
          "next_check": "Use exact source-version equations and, if authorized, a pinned read-only code comparison or defining cited primary source; do not run algorithms.",

    "source_qualifications": {
      "original_dossier": {
        "path": "/private/tmp/aimech-cope2023-formal-model-source-research-20261016/dossier.json",
        "sha256": "6b5992a634cc6edb771a304d6b2716d484c5b7a22bda898786446975ccfdb1fd"
      },
      "all15original_limits_unchanged": [
        {
          "id": "L01",
          "text": "Static supplied-distribution abstraction; online estimation and integration into a real planner are future work in this paper.",
          "locator": "Official pp.2,8"
        },
        {
          "id": "L02",
          "text": "Sequential known-duration base actions and meta-level uncertainty do not cover arbitrary parallel multi-robot or stochastic-action execution.",
          "locator": "Official pp.1,4,8"
        },
        {
          "id": "L03",
          "text": "Independence is an analysis premise, not a demonstrated property of real search subtrees; product-failure formulas do not survive arbitrary dependencies.",
          "locator": "Official pp.2–4"
        },
        {
          "id": "L04",
          "text": "With a standard CDF,1−D(t) means deadline>t, whereas the induced-deadline derivation prints start(beta)<=X−R. Discrete equality cases need an explicit convention; no silent off-by-one correction is made.",
          "locator": "Official p.3 Eq1 versus p.4; arXiv p.9"
        },
        {
          "id": "L05",
          "text": "The literal arXiv earliest-time expression adds W and a new computation unit although those can overlap. The W=1, empty-tail, one-unit-remaining-computation hand case finishes atT+1 under the printed state updates but formula givesT+2. This is a source-interface discrepancy, not a diagnosed code defect.",
          "locator": "ArXiv p.9 Appendix A"
        },
        {
          "id": "L06",
          "text": "Official Algorithm3 prints no increment in its common-prefix loop, no explicit second-head-length guard and no complete no-mismatch/empty-head convention. Eq7 likewise needs sentinel/empty-set handling for fully compatible heads.",
          "locator": "Official pp.5,7"
        },
        {
          "id": "L07",
          "text": "Demand-Execution indexes the head by W[S] in both official and arXiv displays, although W is remaining time and L is initiated-action count. Keep this mismatch explicit rather than inventing an executable replacement.",
          "locator": "Official pp.5,7; arXiv pp.8–10"
        },
        {
          "id": "L08",
          "text": "Increasing start times alone do not enforce duration-dependent nonoverlap; Algorithm2 omits an explicit feasibility filter. Algorithm4 subtracts an action entry H[j], requiring duration interpretation; guards for short heads, empty heads and absent support minima are not fully printed.",
          "locator": "Official pp.4,6–7"
        },
        {
          "id": "L09",
          "text": "The reduction helper omits D from its explicit arguments while effective deadlines depend on induced deadlines. Ambient state/distribution access, probability-return contracts and all-zero-success behavior need implementation clarification.",
          "locator": "Official pp.6–7 Algorithms1–5"
        },
        {
          "id": "L10",
          "text": "Hazard denominators require unfinished-process positive survival, log-failure utility needs zero/one boundary handling, and LPF/t requires positive allocation time. The formulas are not a complete numerically guarded implementation.",
          "locator": "Official pp.3,5"
        },
        {
          "id": "L11",
          "text": "General CoPE/KID-CoPE are not claimed polynomial-time solvable. The exact cases are pseudo-polynomial in numeric horizons/explicit distributions with bounded-prefix or equal-slack restrictions; bounded truncation in the general case gives up optimality.",
          "locator": "Official pp.5–6"
        },
        {
          "id": "L12",
          "text": "The arXiv proof sketches were read but not formally verified. Their model and interface premises must remain attached; no theorem certification or extension to arbitrary dependencies/continuous time is claimed.",
          "locator": "ArXiv p.9 Appendix B"
        },
        {
          "id": "L13",
          "text": "The original author PDF lacks the cited appendix, while official and arXiv have different algorithm displays. The code URL is retained but no code was downloaded, audited or executed.",
          "locator": "Author p.5; official pp.5–7; arXiv pp.9–10"
        },
        {
          "id": "L14",
          "text": "Reported outcomes are setting-specific simulations. Profile calibration, finite data uncertainty, runtime overhead in a continuously updating planner and paired statistical significance are not established here.",
          "locator": "Official pp.7–8; arXiv pp.10–13"
        },
        {
          "id": "L15",
          "text": "Refined-Max-LET/IPAE names in arXiv are not asserted aliases of K-Bounded/CoPE. A publication/version label or base-algorithm choice is not automatically a separate AI concept.",
          "locator": "ArXiv p.10 versus official pp.6–7"
        }
      ],

  "entries": [
    {
      "path": "data/curated/ConcurrentPlanningExecutionModel.yaml",
      "disposition": "added",
      "id": "AIMech:ConcurrentPlanningExecutionModel",
      "name": "Concurrent planning and execution metareasoning model",
      "definition": "A formal metareasoning model that represents competing plan-computation processes, their known executable action heads and induced-deadline distributions, and poses the problem of selecting a joint computation/execution policy to maximize timely solution probability in the source’s concurrent-planning setting.",
      "concept_kind": "model_family",
      "aliases": [],
      "identity_notes": "The source-specific formal decision model for concurrent planning and execution, with planning-process performance profiles, known action heads, induced deadlines and a joint computation/execution policy objective. Retain one named formal model. Its problem statement and MDP encoding are representations of the same scoped subject; do not create separate identities for the encoding or every assumption-restricted subcase. General Definition 1, the four simplifying analysis assumptions, and KID-CoPE special-case results are distinct layers. This is not a claim that every instance has the properties of the restricted MDP analysis. CoPE is used for a broader setting and in the 2025 source; omit it as a global alias. The descriptive canonical name narrows this proposal to the 2023 metareasoning model. Current insertion identity was assessed on 2026-10-16 at merged HEAD 8650bfb55ef0c67902b5a80f1527920c87ad1d9d and tree cd6972cabe7b7f1cdf9ca5ee69bd6263a991ba50. The complete inventory contains813 maintained and442 pinned AIO records,1255 total, with no normalized collision among the four candidates. Eight ignored- and hidden-inclusive searches across data/, research/, sources/ and docs/ account for167 distinct matching contents and856 match events. Of these,105 groups retain exact historical scoped-event attribution and62 contents received fresh semantic reading with complete relevant parent context. The newly added manufacturing record was fully compared;22 prior native contexts are byte-identical and retain attributed semantic comparisons. The current mapping assessment read21 complete pinned AIO nodes and72 incident edges. The peer independently checked the current-state work with original scientific authorship disclosed. This is bounded identity clearance for the selected corpus and pin, not universal novelty or source exhaustion. Historical131-content/588-occurrence searching used four whole checkouts and included review/vendor contexts; it is retained by attribution rather than described as the current four-root search. The existing main911 source coordinator is accepted for this insertion without merging method identities or closing source questions.",
      "definition_evidence": [
        {
          "source_id": "elboher2023",
          "locator": "Official PDF p.4 Definition 1 and action/deadline formalization; pp.4–5 Section 3.1.",
          "relation": "supports"
        }
      ],
      "claims": [
        {
          "claim_id": "formal-input-and-objective",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "The CoPE problem supplies a set of base actions with positive durations and n planning processes. Each process has a possibly empty known action head H_i, a computation-completion performance profile M_i and an induced-deadline distribution D_i. A policy allocates computation and legally initiates head actions to maximize the probability of executing a timely solution. The model is a static decision abstraction rather than a single search procedure.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.4, Definition 1 and surrounding formalization; pp.1–2 motivation.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "serial-actions-and-prefix-invalidation",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "A legal initiated prefix starts no earlier than time zero, starts each later action no earlier than the preceding action finishes, and respects operative individual action deadlines. Base actions are non-preemptible and cannot execute in parallel, while computation can overlap a base action. Executing a prefix invalidates a process whose known head is incompatible with that prefix. The unknown suffix cannot start before its planning process terminates.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.4, action legality, non-preemption, incompatibility and suffix-start paragraphs.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "induced-deadline-construction",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "For process i, let X_i be the time by which the complete solution must finish and R_i the unknown remainder duration revealed when planning terminates. The source defines the induced deadline as D_i=X_i−R_i and writes timely suffix initiation as start(beta_i)<=X_i−R_i. This subtraction is meaningful even when X_i and R_i are dependent. The later mutual-independence premise for the M_i and induced D_i variables is separate from this definition.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.4, induced-deadline derivation preceding Definition 1.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "restricted-analysis-assumptions",
          "kind": "scope",
          "statement": "The analyzed construction assumes discrete time, known action durations, mutual independence of all performance-profile and induced-deadline variables, and no operative individual base-action deadlines. Positive base-action durations are already part of Definition 1. The statement that an implementation can allow individual action deadlines does not extend the displayed analyses to all such cases.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.4, four simplifying assumptions after Example2, with Definition 1.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "decision-state-and-computation-transition",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "The analyzed MDP records wall time T, computation already allocated to each process and its failure state, remaining execution time W for the current base action, and the number L of initiated or completed base actions, with terminal SUCCESS and FAIL states. A computation action allocates one unit to an eligible process; conditional on unfinished positive survival, its termination probability is m_i(T_i+1)/(1−M_i(T_i)). Computation advances wall time while an executing base action can progress. Base initiation is allowed only when no other base action is executing and the action is next in a surviving head. The source assigns reward one to SUCCESS and zero elsewhere.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF pp.4–5, Section 3.1 state, transition, reward and eligibility descriptions.",
              "relation": "supports"
            },
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023-arxiv",
              "locator": "arXiv v1 PDF pp.8–9, Appendix A, state variables and computation/base-action transition equations.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "known-deadline-policy-results",
          "kind": "scope",
          "statement": "For KID-CoPE, the known-induced-deadline restriction under the stated analysis assumptions, the source states that policies are linear and that an optimal policy exists which is linear, computation-contiguous and lazy. Contiguity applies to the computation subsequence CA(sigma), so base-action initiations may still intervene. Laziness delays base initiations until a further adjacent delay would be tardy or illegal. These are source-stated restricted existence results, not a claim that every policy is optimal or that the general heuristic schemes solve all CoPE instances optimally.",
          "evidence": [
            {

      "definition": "A computation-focused CoPE next-action schema that consults a supplied computation allocator and substitutes a required head action when its latest-start timeliness test demands execution, otherwise returning the recommended computation action.",
      "concept_kind": "algorithm",
      "aliases": [],
      "identity_notes": "The official computation-focused Demand-Execution_A next-action schema: consult a supplied computation allocator, then initiate a required next head action when the timeliness condition demands execution. Retain the named schema; solver A and its configured policies are parameters. The printed W[S] index versus remaining-time meaning, availability of the next head action and other literal interface conditions remain unresolved. Do not treat the display as a certified implementation or import a general optimality theorem. Use the CoPE-qualified descriptive name, aliases[].       ],
      "claims": [
        {
          "claim_id": "computation-first-recommendation",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "Demand-Execution_A first uses a supplied S(AE)^2 algorithm A to choose the next process computation under the assumption that no base-level actions are executed before computation terminates. The source then tests whether a base action is required to keep that recommended process non-tardy, rather than first fixing and comparing complete head-initiation policies.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.6, Section 6 computation-focused schemes and Demand-Execution paragraph.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "timeliness-triggered-base-action",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "For the recommended process, the displayed rule selects the minimum support value of its induced-deadline distribution and constructs latest head-start times. It compares a selected head action’s scheduled start to the current wall time and returns that base action when the equality test holds; otherwise it returns the recommended computation action. The identity concerns this timeliness-triggered choice, while the printed head-index convention is retained as an unresolved interface limitation.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF p.7, Algorithms 4–5; p.6 Demand-Execution prose.",
              "relation": "supports"
            },
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023-arxiv",
              "locator": "arXiv v1 PDF p.9, Appendix A transition/timeliness expression; p.10, older Demand-Execution display. Context for the retained overlap and W-index interface limitations, not evidence of exact version equivalence.",
              "relation": "context"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "next-action-schema-output",
          "kind": "scope",
          "statement": "The official display returns one base-level or computation action for the current state. It is a parameterized next-action selector within CoPE, unlike the execution-focused schemas which construct and compare combined policies. It neither defines the supplied allocator A nor supplies a general optimality theorem, a learned policy or the later2025dual-open-list planner.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "elboher2023",
              "locator": "Official PDF pp.6–7, Section 6 contrast and Algorithm 5 result declaration.",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The selector operates in the source static CoPE abstraction with supplied distributions and sequential non-preemptible base actions. It does not provide online profile learning, full planner integration, arbitrary parallel-action execution or a stochastic physical-action model.",
        "The supplied allocator and timeliness tests retain their probability premises. Independence is an analysis assumption, and strict deadline survival from1−D(t) differs from the inclusive induced-deadline derivation at atoms. An explicit boundary convention is required before executable interpretation.",
        "Algorithm 5 assigns index=W[S], although the MDP defines W as remaining duration of the currently executing base action and L as the number of initiated/completed actions. The arXiv display retains the same issue. The draft does not substitute L or another index and does not diagnose the linked implementation.",
        "The display does not fully specify eligibility when an action is already executing, absent/empty head positions, a completed head, exhausted policy output or no feasible process. The model’s legal-action rules still apply. Latest-time scheduling uses duration shorthand and requires support-minimum and nonnegative/feasible-start conventions.",
        "The arXiv earliest-time/timeliness transition expression can add W and a computation unit that overlap under its own progress updates. The retained W=1, one-unit remaining computation and empty unstarted-head case gives completion atT+1 in the updates versusT+2 in the expression. This limits a literal interpretation of model-based tardiness without asserting that Demand-Execution code has that behavior.",
        "The allocation subroutine must declare its state/probability/policy-return contract. Conditional hazard denominators need unfinished positive survival, log-failure utilities need zero/one boundary treatment and LPF/time scores need positive time. None is certified by the wrapper’s call to A.",
        "Demand-Execution is one of the source’s general-case suboptimal schemes. KID-CoPE structural existence results and pseudo-polynomial exact cases concern different restricted conditions and do not prove this computation-first rule optimal or complete. The arXiv proofs were read without formal verification.",
        "Official Algorithm 5 and the arXiv older-naming display remain version-specific evidence, with unresolved interface correspondence. Refined-Max-LET/IPAE and the2021 route are not accepted aliases of this selector or of CoPE generally. The author main PDF lacks the referenced appendix; no code was downloaded or run.",
        "Configured simulations over15-puzzle-derived profiles, chosen solvers and action durations do not establish calibrated success estimates, universal runtime advantage, statistical significance or practical online-planning overhead. Instance ellipses and rounded small runtimes are not confidence intervals or exact measurements."
